title: [P1] Database writes failing — transaction log volume exhausted

title: [P1] API gateway health checks failing — file descriptor exhaustion

failure.root_cause_statement: api-gateway is leaking file descriptors because a middleware added in v8.1.0 opens connections to config-service on every request but never closes them when the request errors, causing the FD limit of 65536 to be reached over 6 hours of gradual accumulation and making the gateway unable to accept new connections

red_herrings.description: config-service shows a massive spike in active connections that looks like it is under attack or overloaded — it is the recipient of all leaked connections and is technically healthy, just overwhelmed by open but idle sockets

health-check-aggregator reports all services as unhealthy because api-gateway cannot open new connections to respond to health probes — aggregator reports widespread failure but the failure is entirely within api-gateway

title: [P0] Data pipeline silent corruption — downstream consumers receiving malformed events

failure.root_cause_statement: stream-processor v4.0.0 upgraded its Avro serialization library from avro-python3 1.11.0 to 1.11.3 which changed the default null handling for union types, causing records with optional fields to be serialized with null bytes in different positions than schema-registry expects, producing deserialization errors in data-lake-writer and consumer-api while event-ingestion and schema-registry appear completely healthy

red_herrings.description: dlq-handler shows extremely high processing volume because all corrupted records are being routed to the dead letter queue — it looks overloaded and broken but is functioning correctly, just processing 100x its normal volume

schema-registry shows elevated schema validation errors which appear to be the cause of the corruption — but schema-registry is correct, it is downstream deserialization that fails because the bytes no longer match the registered schema format

event-ingestion metrics are completely nominal and its logs show no errors — this makes operators assume the problem is downstream and spend time investigating data-lake-writer when the corruption was introduced by stream-processor

title: [P0] Duplicate writes and data inconsistency — write conflict storm

failure.root_cause_statement: a network partition lasting 45 seconds caused consensus-service to lose quorum and elect replica-db as a second primary, creating a split-brain condition where both primary-db and replica-db accepted writes for 3 minutes before the partition healed and conflict detection surfaced thousands of write conflicts requiring manual resolution

red_herrings.description: monitoring-probe flagged a network blip 9 minutes ago and auto-resolved it — operators dismiss it as a transient monitoring false-positive when it was actually the network partition that triggered the split-brain

application-server shows duplicate record errors and constraint violations that look like an application-layer bug or race condition — the duplicates are actually caused by two database primaries accepting the same writes

replica-db shows unusually high write throughput and primary-level behavior that should be suspicious but can be mistaken for a replication catch-up after lag — it has actually been elected as a rogue primary

title: [P0] Complete service mesh freeze — all requests hanging indefinitely

failure.root_cause_statement: a distributed lock contention created a circular wait: service-a holds lock L1 and waits for lock L2, service-b holds lock L2 and waits for lock L3, service-c holds lock L3 and waits for lock L1, creating a system-wide deadlock that causes all three services to hang indefinitely since lock-manager has no deadlock detection timeout configured

red_herrings.description: circuit-breaker-proxy opens all circuit breakers after 30 seconds of upstream timeouts, producing a cascade of CIRCUIT_OPEN alerts that make it appear the services themselves are crashing or overloaded when they are actually deadlocked waiting for locks

api-router shows 100% request timeout rate and logs suggest it is dropping all connections, making it look like the router is misconfigured or overloaded — it is healthy but all requests hang waiting for the deadlocked services

service-b is the most visible hung service because it sits in the middle of the dependency chain and both service-a and service-c reference it in their timeout logs — but all three services are equally deadlocked
